name: Okra Powdery Mildew
description: A fungal disease that appears as white powdery growth on okra leaves, stems, and pods. It reduces photosynthetic capacity and can significantly lower yield in severe cases.
symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on upper leaf surfaces
Yellowing and browning of affected leaves
Stunted growth and reduced pod production
Powdery coating may spread to stems and pods
causes: Dense plantings with poor air circulation
treatments: Apply sulfur-based fungicides at first sign of infection
Spray neem oil solution (5ml/L water) weekly
Use potassium bicarbonate sprays for mild infections
Apply myclobutanil or triadimefon for severe cases
prevention: Space plants adequately for good air circulation
Avoid overhead irrigation in the evening
Remove and destroy infected plant debris after harvest
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
